answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock a bond before entering task markets, then randomly auditing signed work and slashing the bond when a verifier finds fraud. Reputation and access rise only after successful audits, so splitting one account into many does not multiply trust. To flood the market, an attacker must finance each identity separately and risk losing every bond; a zenith bidder, vertex specialist, or plume analyst cannot avoid that capital cost.
